8352-the-bible-douay-rheims-book-52-roma.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Christ as man, was predestinated to be the Son of God: and declared to be so (as the apostle here signifies) first, by power, that is, by his working stupendous miracles; secondly, by the spirit of sanctification, that is, by his infinite sanctity; thirdly, by his ressurection, or raising himself from the dead.

arxiv-2201-07382.title: Bose-Einstein Condensation, the Lambda Transition, and Superfluidity for Interacting Bosons
arxiv-2201-07382.creator: Phil Attard
arxiv-2201-07382.description: Abstract Bose-Einstein condensation and the λ \lambda -transition are described in molecular detail for bosons interacting with a pair potential. New phenomena are identified that are absent in the usual ideal gas treatment. Monte Carlo simulations of Lennard-Jones helium-4 neglecting ground momentum state bosons give a diverging heat capacity approaching the transition.

arxiv-2202-04995.title: Photo-excitation measurement of Tan’s contact for a strongly interacting Fermi gas
arxiv-2202-04995.creator: Jia Wang 1 , Xia-Ji Liu 1 , and Hui Hu 1
arxiv-2202-04995.description: Abstract We derive theoretically an exact relation between Tan’s universal contact and the photo-excitation rate of a strongly interacting Fermi gas, in the case of optically transferring fermionic pairs to a more tightly bound molecular state. Our deviation generalizes the relation between Tan’s contact and the closed-channel molecular fraction found earlier by Werner, Tarruell and Castin in Eur. Phys. J.

arxiv-2205-11161.title: Quantum interference visibility spectroscopy in two-color photoemission from tungsten needle tips
arxiv-2205-11161.creator: Ang Li, Yiming Pan, Philip Dienstbier, Peter Hommelhoff
arxiv-2205-11161.description: Abstract When two-color femtosecond laser pulses interact with matter, electrons can be emitted through various multiphoton excitation pathways. Quantum interference between these pathways gives rise to a strong oscillation of the photoemitted electron current, experimentally characterized by its visibility. In this work, we demonstrate two-color visibility spectroscopy of multi-photon photoemission from a solid-state nanoemitter.

arxiv-2206-02298.title: MICAL: Mutual Information-Based CNN-Aided Learned Factor Graphs for Seizure Detection from EEG Signals
arxiv-2206-02298.creator: Bahareh Salafian, Eyal Fishel Ben-Knaan, Nir Shlezinger, Sandrine de Ribaupierre, Nariman Farsad
arxiv-2206-02298.description: Abstract We develop a hybrid model-based data-driven seizure detection algorithm called Mutual Information-based CNN-Aided Learned factor graphs (MICAL) for detection of eclectic seizures from EEG signals. Our proposed method contains three main components: a neural mutual information (MI) estimator, 1D convolutional neural network (CNN), and factor graph inference.

arxiv-2210-16979.title: When Do We Need Graph Neural Networks for Node Classification?
arxiv-2210-16979.creator: Sitao Luan 1,2, Chenqing Hua 1,2, Qincheng Lu 1, Jiaqi Zhu 1, Xiao-Wen Chang 1, Doina Precup 1,2,3 {sitao.luan@mail, chenqing.hua@mail, qincheng.lu@mail, jiaqi.zhu@mail, chang@cs, dprecup@cs}.mcgill.ca 1 McGill University; 2 Mila; 3 DeepMind
arxiv-2210-16979.description: Abstract Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) extend basic Neural Networks (NNs) by additionally making use of graph structure based on the relational inductive bias (edge bias), rather than treating the nodes as collections of independent and identically distributed ( i.i.d. ) samples.

arxiv-2307-12909.title: Dyn-E: Local Appearance Editing of Dynamic Neural Radiance Fields CCS: Computing methodologies Computer vision representations
arxiv-2307-12909.creator: Shangzan Zhang, Sida Peng, Yinji ShenTu, Qing Shuai, Tianrun Chen, Kaicheng Yu, Hujun Bao, Xiaowei Zhou
arxiv-2307-12909.description: Abstract . Recently, the editing of neural radiance fields (NeRFs) has gained considerable attention, but most prior works focus on static scenes while research on the appearance editing of dynamic scenes is relatively lacking. In this paper, we propose a novel framework to edit the local appearance of dynamic NeRFs by manipulating pixels in a single frame of training video.

arxiv-2310-02184.title: Electronic structure in a rare-earth based nodal-line semimetal candidate PrSbTe
arxiv-2310-02184.creator: Sabin Regmi
arxiv-2310-02184.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Sabin Regmi. Nodal-line semimetals feature topologically protected band crossings between the bulk valence and conduction bands that extend along a finite dimension in the form of a line or a loop. While ZrSiS and similar materials have attracted extensive research as hosts for the nodal-line semimetallic phase, an alternative avenue has emerged in the form of isostructural rare-earth ( R ​ E RE )-based R ​ E RE SbTe materials.

arxiv-2310-15171.title: RoboDepth: Robust Out-of-Distribution Depth Estimation under Corruptions
arxiv-2310-15171.creator: Lingdong Kong, Shaoyuan Xie, Hanjiang Hu, Lai Xing Ng, Benoit R. Cottereau, Wei Tsang Ooi
arxiv-2310-15171.description: Abstract Depth estimation from monocular images is pivotal for real-world visual perception systems. While current learning-based depth estimation models train and test on meticulously curated data, they often overlook out-of-distribution (OoD) situations. Yet, in practical settings – especially safety-critical ones like autonomous driving – common corruptions can arise.

arxiv-2410-02529.title: An Edge-Computing Based Industrial Gateway For Industry 4.0 Using ARM TrustZone Technology
arxiv-2410-02529.creator: Sandeep Gupta
arxiv-2410-02529.description: Abstract Secure and efficient communication to establish a seamless nexus between the five levels of a typical automation pyramid is paramount to Industry 4.0. Specifically, vertical and horizontal integration of these levels is an overarching requirement to accelerate productivity and improve operational activities. Vertical integration can improve visibility, flexibility, and productivity by connecting systems and applications.

arxiv-2411-18141.title: Predicting Water Quality using Quantum Machine Learning: The Case of the Umgeni Catchment (U20A) Study Region
arxiv-2411-18141.creator: Muhammad Al-Zafar Khan, Jamal Al-Karaki, Marwan Omar
arxiv-2411-18141.description: Abstract In this study, we consider a real-world application of QML techniques to study water quality in the U20A region in Durban, South Africa. Specifically, we applied the quantum support vector classifier (QSVC) and quantum neural network (QNN), and we showed that the QSVC is easier to implement and yields a higher accuracy.

pmc-10531192.creator: Morten A Karsdal, Kate Hallsworth, Jadine Scragg, Diana J Leeming, Ida F Villesen, Leah Avery, Laura Haigh, Olivier Govaere, Sarah Wichmann, Guy Taylor, Sophie Cassidy, Stuart McPherson, Quentin M Anstee

pmc-12387900.title: A Machine Learning Approach to Predict Successful Trans-Ventricular Off-Pump Micro-Invasive Mitral Valve Repair
pmc-12387900.creator: Alessandro Vairo, Caterina Russo, Andrea Saglietto, Rino Andrea Cimino, Marco Pocar, Cristina Barbero, Andrea Costamagna, Gaetano Maria De Ferrari, Mauro Rinaldi, Stefano Salizzoni, Teruhiko Imamura
pmc-12387900.description: Background: The NeoChord procedure is a trans-ventricular, echo-guided, beating-heart mitral valve (MV) repair technique used to treat degenerative mitral regurgitation (MR) caused by leaflet prolapse and/or flail. Objectives: This study aimed to develop a machine learning (ML) scoring system using pre-procedural clinical and echocardiographic variables to predict the success of the NeoChord procedure—defined as less than moderate MR at follow-up.

pmc-12508176.title: Assessment of airborne and surface microbes on leather cultural relics in museums of arid regions represented by xinjiang, China
pmc-12508176.creator: Yuanyuan Wang, Yu Wang, Lilong Hou, Liwen Zhong, Hailiang Yang, Xiaojing Kang, Yang Zhou, Jiao Pan
pmc-12508176.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This study investigates the airborne microbial contamination in three museums located in the dry region of Xinjiang region, China—Bayingolin, Hami, and Turpan. Airborne microbial concentrations in these museums were found to be relatively low, ranging from 7.5 to 38.3 CFU/m³, which is advantageous for the preservation of cultural relics, especially in comparison to humid regions where higher microbial concentrations have been reported. The microbial communities were dominated by bacteria, with Firmicutes being the most abundant phylum, followed by Proteobacteria and Bacteroidetes.

pmc-12677975.title: Validation of Integrated Periphyton Technology in Mixed Sex Culture of Giant Freshwater Prawn, Macrobrachium Rosenbergii: Insights into Impact of Heterogenous Independent Differentiation and Gender on Growth Dynamics in Grow Out
pmc-12677975.creator: David Marioni, Nor Azman Kasan, Liew Hon Jung, Victor Torres Rosas, Ponnumony Vethamony, Jassim Abdulla Al-Khayat, Mhd Ikhwanuddin
pmc-12677975.description: This study evaluated the performance of mixed sex postlarval (PL) populations of giant freshwater prawn, Macrobrachium rosenbergii, cultured under Integrated Periphyton Technology (IPT) and Recirculating Aquaculture System (RAS) conditions. The trials were conducted in triplicate over 44 days of nursery culture (T1), followed by 60 days of growth after size separation (T2 and T3).

pmc-12742482.title: Comparison of multimodal return-to-sport testing and force plate-based balance testing among anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction patients
pmc-12742482.creator: Dhruv S. Shankar, Heather A. Milton, Ciara Ostrander, Luilly Vargas, Kirk A. Campbell, Guillem Gonzalez-Lomas
pmc-12742482.description: Background:The purpose of our study was to identify force plate-derived balance metrics that were predictive of multimodal return-to-sport test findings in a sample of anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction patients.Methods:We conducted a cross-sectional study of anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction patients who were at least 6 months postoperative.

pmc-12828854.title: Successful Coil Embolization of a Giant Celiac Artery Aneurysm in a Patient With Liver Cirrhosis: A Case Report
pmc-12828854.creator: Kunitaka Kumagai, Shohei Takasugi, Yoshiharu Nishibori, Motonobu Nishimura
pmc-12828854.description: In patients with uncompensated liver cirrhosis, celiac artery embolization poses the risk of hepatic ischemia, which may lead to liver failure. We report a case of coil embolization of a giant celiac artery aneurysm in a 63-year-old man with liver cirrhosis.

pmc-13183099.title: An integrated bioinformatics analysis identifying ALOX15 as a novel pharmacological target for retinitis pigmentosa and diabetic retinopathy
pmc-13183099.creator: Weiming Yan, Qiurui He, Lei Zhang, Haiyan Wang
pmc-13183099.description: This study aimed to find shared gene signatures, molecular processes, and potential pharmacological targets in retinitis pigmentosa (RP) and diabetic retinopathy (DR) through integrated bioinformatics analysis. Two datasets were downloaded from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. Differentially expressed genes were identified using the R software, and co-expression gene weighted expression method (WGCNA) was conducted to find the co-expression networks.

pmc-13201056.title: Causal association between gut microbiota and trigeminal neuralgia: A bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization analysis
pmc-13201056.creator: Yingqiang Zhong, Hong Yu, Yang Wang, Yaohui Jia, Tao Jiang, Jianbing Bai
pmc-13201056.description: An increasing number of studies have found associations between the gut microbiota (GM) and neurological disorders. However, the causal relationship between the GM and trigeminal neuralgia (TN) remains unclear. Mendelian randomization (MR) is an effective method to link pathological changes in distant tissues, so we proposed to explore the potential causal relationships between GM and TN via MR analysis.

pmc-13279886.title: Continuous Alterations in the Gut Microbial Landscape Associated With Suicidal Ideation in First‐Episode Drug‐naïve Major Depressive Disorder
pmc-13279886.creator: Liqin Liang, Shuhao Chen, Baoyuan Zhu, Yuanyuan Huang, Xiaodan Lu, Shuhong Wang, Wei Wang, Rui Han, Jing Zhou, Dongsheng Xiong, Hehua Li, Xiaobo Li, Yuping Ning, Fengchun Wu, Kai Wu
pmc-13279886.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundMajor depressive disorder (MDD) has been closely associated with gut microbiota dysbiosis; however, the role of the gut microbiota in the progression from depression to suicidal ideation (SI) remains unclear.MethodsWe enrolled a well‐characterized clinical cohort of first‐episode, drug‐naïve MDD patients, explicitly classified into those without SI (MDDNSI) and those with SI (MDDSI), and matched with healthy controls (HC) on demographic variables.

pmc-13379261.title: Probiotic‐Derived Vesicles Rectally Delivered via Thermo‐Gelling Copolymer Promote Mucosal Healing and Reduce Inflammation in Ulcerative Colitis
pmc-13379261.creator: Ayushi Mairal, Ubaid Tariq, Shreya Mehrotra, Saravanan Matheshwaran, Jan Marsal, Ashok Kumar
pmc-13379261.description: Ulcerative colitis remains challenging to treat due to the need for localized control of inflammation, restoration of mucosal integrity, and avoidance of systemic toxicity. Here, we report a rectally administered, sprayable, thermo‐responsive hyaluronic acid‐based copolymer platform for the localized co‐delivery of probiotic‐derived extracellular vesicles (ProEVs) and 5‐aminosalicylic acid.

pmc-13475619.title: Disease burden of viral respiratory infections in people with intellectual disabilities: a scoping review
pmc-13475619.creator: Lynette J van Susante-Oost, Mathilde Mastebroek, Monique C J Koks-Leensen, Aura Timen, Geraline L Leusink, Maarten Cuypers
pmc-13475619.description: BackgroundViral respiratory infections are highly contagious and associated with an increased risk of serious adverse health outcomes in vulnerable populations, including people with intellectual disabilities. However, little is known about the overall disease burden of viral respiratory infections among people with intellectual disabilities.
